thread:
Maria: weekly check-in for Brightleaf — quick summary: usage +12% w/w, spend +18% (billing spike on 3/18), average token rate steady but per-request cost up. Model mix shift: customer moved 60% of traffic to rwd-medium-v2 last Thurs. Fallbacks to rwd-base-v1 spiked to 7.4% from 0.9%.
Ajay: thanks — do we know why fallbacks jumped? config/policy or infra? :thinking_face:
Maria: looks like two simultaneous things: 1) increased request concurrency (they enabled larger batch_size in their client) and 2) a handful of 5xxs during peak windows. fallback traces attached inline.
Maria: snippet of error pattern:
```
2024-03-18T14:03:12Z 500 RuntimeError: CUDA OOM during forward
model=rwd-medium-v2; shard=2; seq_len=1024
```
Kevin: saw the same in infra alerts. NV memory pressure + preemption events on the dedicated pool. queues backed up so router hit fallback policy to base model. I'm going to pin Brightleaf routes to our slow-but-stable pool for the next 6h while we investigate.
Sasha: renewal health check — does this make Brightleaf a risk? they were on track for expansion next quarter.
Maria: short answer: risk = low->medium. They saw value (usage up) but the cost spike and occasional regressions raised concern. CS is scheduling an enablement call tomorrow to review client batching and recommend quantization settings.
Ajay: can we produce a small runbook for them? quick wins: cap concurrency, set max_batch_size=8, enable kv-prefix-cache for repeated prompts, downgrade to rwd-small-v2 for non-critical routes.
Maria: yes. I'll draft runbook and share before the call.
health-bot: automated weekly health report for Brightleaf (last 7d): requests=1.2M, errors=0.8%, fallback_rate=7.4%, avg_latency=210ms (+85ms), spend=$4.2k (+18%). Top error = CUDA OOM (rwd-medium-v2). Link: https://console.redwood.ai/customers/brightleaf/health
Kevin: action item for eng-runtime: investigate kernel memory fragmentation when sequence lengths >512. tagging @eng-runtime and @eng-infra.
Ajay: ping @product for a possible temporary feature flag to reduce concurrency when fallback_rate >5%.
Sasha: noted — CS will lead the customer sync, ask eng for a short tech brief we can share.
Maria: next steps: (1) Kevin to pin pool (done), (2) Maria to send runbook + schedule call, (3) Ajay to scope product flag, (4) monitor fallback_rate hourly and report to #customer-success. I'll post a follow-up snapshot in 24h.
Kevin: I'll also surface kernel-level traces and the OOM sample logs to the runtime team.
Sasha: thanks all. :thumbsup:
Maria: ack. will update thread after the call.
health-bot: note: follow-up reminder set for 1850004722 (24h).
